summary: The browser is started once and kept, instead of a fresh node+Chrome per batch of pages. A full check of the eleven sample diagrams starts 5 browsers where it started 31, for the same 31 batches and the same 112 layout candidates, and takes 12.4s where it took 23.9s. Nothing rendered differently.
why: Starting Chrome costs about twenty times what inspecting one more page in a running one does, and the renderer's work arrives as many small batches — a note's anchors, a spacing rung, a gate — so a process per batch spent most of a check booting. Two counts were also wrong and are fixed here: browser starts were counted where a batch was sent rather than where a browser is built, which reported 31 for a check that starts 5, and each repeat of a job now begins with no browser so its time is one a real command can achieve.
